ALWAYS snapshot the release book (SearchReleaseGrid) before any production write. It IS the restore source - re-POST backup rows verbatim to un-cancel, cancel any ReleaseNo not in backup. Saved us when the demand bug hit.
Never trust a Success:true response. Verify every write by fresh reload and check actual values. Test showed ok:true while forecast releases silently regenerated.

Write per-part ATOMIC (cancel old + place new in ONE UpdateReleaseGrid POST). A mid-run failure then leaves every unprocessed part on its original working releases. Break on 419/401/403 to avoid partial state.

Rows with a ReleaseNo = real PO releases (cancellable, stick). Rows without = MRP forecast projections, NOT cancellable - MRP regenerates them. Forecast over-supply is a forecast/lot-size settings fix, not a release fix.
PO API (UpdateReleaseGrid) can set DueDate inside the frozen window AND hold Firm at any horizon - the MRP release screen cannot (it clamps to Forecast beyond firm-days and one-release-per-week).
Dry-run first on production: compute schedules and print projected inventory with NO writes, confirm no part left uncovered and nothing balloons, THEN write.
